title: Low-degree local-cohomology algebraization in a complete local ring
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a nonzero commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], complete for the maximal-ideal adic topology [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let $I\subsetneq A$ be an ideal and let $M$ be a finite $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Work in the ordinary derived category $D(A)$ of $A$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For an ideal $K$, put $\Gamma_K(N)=\{x\in N:K^r x=0\text{ for some }r\geq0\}$ [def-sbc-ideal-power-torsion-functor], and write $R\Gamma_K$ for its right derived functor and $H_K^j(M)=H^j(R\Gamma_K(M[0]))$. Write $L^{\wedge_I}=R\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(L\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A/I^n)$ for derived $I$-adic completion: the derived tensor is computed using a K-flat resolution, and the derived inverse limit [def-weil-derived-limit] using the mapping fibre of $1-\mathrm{shift}$ on the termwise products of a complex-level model of the tower. Use these derived-functor models and their natural completion maps, not arbitrary maps between abstract choices of cones. Fix an integer $q\geq0$ such that $H_I^j(N)=0$ for every $A$-module $N$ and every $j>q$. For every prime $\mathfrak p$ not containing $I$ with $V(\mathfrak p)\cap V(I)\ne\{\mathfrak m\}$ assume $\operatorname{depth}_{A_{\mathfrak p}}M_{\mathfrak p}\geq1$ or $\operatorname{depth}_{A_{\mathfrak p}}M_{\mathfrak p}+\dim\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak p)>q+1$, using regular-sequence depth [def-weil-pbc-depth], localization [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Here $V(K)=\{\mathfrak p:K\subseteq\mathfrak p\}$ in $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Then there exists an ideal $J_0$ with $V(J_0)\cap V(I)=\{\mathfrak m\}$ such that, for every ideal $J\subseteq J_0$ with $V(J)\cap V(I)=\{\mathfrak m\}$, the canonical composite $\alpha_J:R\Gamma_J(M[0])\longrightarrow(R\Gamma_J(M[0]))^{\wedge_I}\cong(R\Gamma_{\mathfrak m}(M[0]))^{\wedge_I}$ induces isomorphisms on $H^0$ and $H^1$. The displayed identification is the natural one from equality of supports after intersecting with $V(I)$.

proof.text: Since $I$ is proper, $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$, and [lem-sbc-complete-local-subideal] makes $A$ $I$-adically complete. The statement of [lem-per-completed-affine-localization-diagram] supplies the natural identification $F_I(R\Gamma_J(N[0]))\cong C(N)=F_I(R\Gamma_{\mathfrak m}(N[0]))$ for every admissible $J$ and finite $N$, with the specified canonical completion map. Exactness and compatibility with triangles can be seen on the models: [lem-per-affine-support-cech-localization] represents $R\Gamma_J$ by tensor with the augmented localization complex, which commutes with cones. Use strict diagram K-flat replacements [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-kflat-replacements]; cones remain K-flat by [lem-pc-kflat-cone-direct-sum]. Tensoring those cones with $A/I^n$ and taking the exact derived tower limit [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] again preserves triangles. The quotient maps $A\to A/I^n$ commute with these constructions, so completion gives morphisms of triangles. The natural support identification above commutes with them. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-cohomology-ladder], every short exact sequence of finite modules therefore gives the commutative comparison of long exact cohomology sequences for $\alpha_J:R\Gamma_J\to C$.

source.place: Tag 0DXP, first paragraph of proof and natural comparison diagrams, using the existing completed localization diagram and the strict derived-functor cone models.

proof.text: We first prove a degree-zero assertion for EVERY finite $N$, without depth hypotheses. Apply [lem-per-local-support-completion-h0] with $J=\mathfrak m$: $H^0(C(N))$ is the union of $H_K^0(N)\subseteq N$ over ideals $K\subseteq\mathfrak m$ with $V(K)\cap V(I)=\{\mathfrak m\}$. This family is directed: replacing two ideals by their product enlarges both torsion submodules and preserves the intersection condition. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finite-module-acc] the family has a maximal member, say $H_{K_N}^0(N)$; directedness makes it equal to the entire union. Hence $H_J^0(N)\to H^0(C(N))$ is an isomorphism whenever $J\subseteq K_N$ is admissible. Indeed $H_{K_N}^0(N)\subseteq H_J^0(N)\subseteq H^0(C(N))$ are inclusions of submodules of $N$. Both functors have zero negative cohomology on $N$, the completed one by the same cited formula.

source.place: Tag 0DXP, degree-zero base case, expanded via Dualizing Complexes Tags 0EEW and 0EEX.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-local-support-finite-submodule-decomposition] to $M$. It gives $0\to P\to M\to B\to0$, an admissible ideal $L$, and an isomorphism $\alpha_J(P)$ in every degree for every admissible $J\subseteq L$. It also gives $P_{\mathfrak p}=0$ and hence $B_{\mathfrak p}=M_{\mathfrak p}$ at every $\mathfrak p\notin T$. Thus $B$ satisfies precisely the stated depth alternative at these primes, and its associated primes are outside $T$. It suffices to prove the degree-one assertion for $B$: the natural long exact sequences from Step 1 have identical $P$ terms, so their kernel/cokernel chase transports any eventual isomorphisms for $B$ to those for $M$. We henceforth prove it for $B$, returning to $M$ in the last step.

The hypotheses of [lem-per-local-support-kill-colimit] hold for $B$ with $s=1$ and $d=q$. To verify the isolated-intersection dimension hypothesis, [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-finite-krull-dimension] makes $\dim A$ finite, and [lem-per-isolated-intersection-dimension-bound] gives $\dim(A/\mathfrak p)\leq\operatorname{cd}(A,I)\leq q$. The last inequality is exactly the stipulated uniform vanishing above $q$. Obtain an admissible $J_1$ and $t\geq1$ such that all admissible $J\subseteq J_1$ have $H^1_{J_1}(B)\cong H^1_J(B)$ and $(J_1I)^tH^1_J(B)=0$. No identification with $H^1_{\mathfrak m}(B)$ and no annihilation by a power of $I$ alone is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0DXP, application of Tag 0DXM; isolated-intersection hypothesis verified by Tag 0DXF.

proof.text: For $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Ass}(B)$ choose $0\ne z\in B$ with annihilator $\mathfrak p$. Its localization $z/1$ is nonzero (otherwise an element outside $\mathfrak p$ kills $z$), and is killed by the maximal ideal of $A_{\mathfrak p}$. The localized generators of $B$ generate $B_{\mathfrak p}$, so this is a finite, nonzero local module. By [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-jacobson], its maximal ideal cannot generate the whole module. Consequently no element of that maximal ideal acts injectively on $B_{\mathfrak p}$, so the regular-sequence definition [def-weil-pbc-depth] gives depth zero. Step 3 puts $\mathfrak p$ outside $T$, so the stated depth alternative forces $\dim(A/\mathfrak p)>q+1$. Applying [lem-per-local-support-inductive-nonzerodivisor] with $s=1,d=q$ shows that the ideal $\mathfrak a=\operatorname{Ann}_A H^1(C(B))$ is not contained in any associated prime of $B$.

Each $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Ass}(B)$ avoids $I$, by Step 3. It also cannot contain $J_1$, since that would give $\{\mathfrak m\}\subseteq V(\mathfrak p)\cap V(I)\subseteq V(J_1)\cap V(I)=\{\mathfrak m\}$, contradicting $\mathfrak p
otin T$. For each such prime choose $a\in\mathfrak a\setminus\mathfrak p$, $b\in J_1\setminus\mathfrak p$, and $c\in I\setminus\mathfrak p$; then $a(bc)^t
otin\mathfrak p$. Thus $\mathfrak a(J_1I)^t$ is contained in none of these primes. For $B
e0$ their set is nonempty: $0$ is a zerodivisor and the cited union theorem puts it in an associated prime. Their set is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-associated-primes-finite]. Prime avoidance [lem-weil-pbc-prime-avoidance] gives a single $f\in\mathfrak a(J_1I)^t$ outside their union. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-module-zerodivisors-union-associated-primes], $f$ acts injectively on $B$. It kills $H^1(C(B))$ and every $H_J^1(B)$ for admissible $J\subseteq J_1$. If $B=0$ the comparison is already an isomorphism and no choice of $f$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 0DXP, prime avoidance and uniform choice of f after support stabilization.

proof.text:
Put $D=B/fB$, a finite module, and apply Step 2 to $B,D,M$. Let $J_0=LJ_1K_BK_DK_M$. Every factor has isolated intersection with $V(I)$, so their product does too, since its vanishing set is the union of theirs. For any admissible $J\subseteq J_0$, apply the natural derived-functor transformation of Step 1 to $0\to B\xrightarrow f B\to D\to0$. Because $f$ annihilates the two degree-one groups, the resulting exact rows end in
$$H_J^0(B)\longrightarrow H_J^0(D)\longrightarrow H_J^1(B)\longrightarrow0,\qquad H^0(C(B))\longrightarrow H^0(C(D))\longrightarrow H^1(C(B))\longrightarrow0.$$
The first two vertical arrows are isomorphisms by Step 2, so the induced arrow on cokernels is an isomorphism: this is $H^1(\alpha_J(B))$. Both rows come from the same fixed $f$, chosen before $J_0$, so the conclusion holds for every such $J$.

source.place: Tag 0DXP, final comparison diagram; its degree-one conclusion is an explicit cokernel argument.

proof.text: Finally use $0\to P\to M\to B\to0$. Since $\alpha_J(P)$ is an isomorphism in every degree, the kernels and cokernels of $\alpha_J(M)$ and $\alpha_J(B)$ agree via the natural comparison diagram (equivalently, their mapping cones are isomorphic). Thus Step 7 gives the degree-one isomorphism for $M$. The degree-zero isomorphism follows from $J\subseteq K_M$ in Step 2. All support identifications are those of Step 1 and commute with completion maps. Hence the resulting isomorphisms are induced by the exact canonical composite $\alpha_J$ in the statement being proved.

Each of the eight steps was checked against the 0DXP proof. Step 2 is the degree-0 base case (0EEX union plus ACC and directedness), Step 3 removes the support submodule, Step 4 is 0DXM with s=1, d=q, the dimension hypothesis coming from the finite local Krull dimension and the 0DXF bound. Step 5 gets depth 0 at associated primes (Nakayama rules out the depth-infinity case), then applies 0DXK. Step 6 picks f by prime avoidance in a(J1 I)^t, and f is fixed before J0. Step 7 is the cokernel argument for B/fB. Step 8 is the five lemma using P in all degrees and H0 of B. The four new nodes match 0EEW/0EEX, 0DXM (support maps oriented as inclusions, which is only notation), 0DXK and the support paragraph of 0DXP. The set T is closed under specialization, P is the source's submodule M', and Ass(M/P) misses T. I tested them on k[[x,y]] with I=(x), N=A and N=A/y, on the M=A/(y,z) counterexample, and on M_p=0.
